name: search_notes
title: Search notes
description: Search the notes of every notebook here (pass notebook for one) by their words: "full-text" matches words exactly ("a phrase", prefix*, -excluded, title:word); "hybrid" (the default) is the same here, since a git notebook has no meaning search, and "semantic" is refused. Filter by folderId (with its subfolders), tag (with nested tags) and updated time. Results give each note id, title, a snippet with matches in **bold**, tags, its description when it has one, and when it was last updated; call read_note for the full text.

updatedAfter.description: Only notes edited after this ISO 8601 date or time, e.g. 2026-10-01.

updatedBefore.description: Only notes edited before this ISO 8601 date or time.

notebook.description: The notebook, by its name as Penmoss shows it or by the 4 characters its short ids start with. Leave it out when you name a note or folder by its id: the id finds its notebook. Searches and lists cover every notebook without it. A new note, folder or daily note needs it when more than one notebook is served.

name: read_note
title: Read a note
description: Read a note: its title, tags, headings and markdown body, and its baseVersion. Keep the baseVersion: every edit tool takes it, and update_section and replace_text require it, so an edit only goes ahead if the part you change is still as you read it. Read again before editing if some time has passed. A long body comes in parts of about 60 KB: when truncated is true, call again with offset set to nextOffset, or read just one section with heading. A line may start with symbols, each a glyph and a space after any list marker, checkbox or heading hashes (★ important, ? question, ! follow-up, 💡 idea, → next): plain text the apps draw in the margin; write one the same way to mark a line.

id.description: The note id (26 characters) or its short id (e.g. K7QD-9HTF2CXA), from search_notes, list_recent or list_folder.

heading.description: Read only the section under this heading (e.g. "Plans" or "## Plans").

offset.description: Start here: the nextOffset of the previous part of a long note.

name: list_comment_threads
title: List comment threads
description: List comment threads: on one note (id), or across the notes. The user comments on a passage or a point of a note, often to ask you for something ("make this tighter"); you can reply, resolve, and start threads of your own (for example to review passages). status is open by default; resolved threads are kept for good. sentToMe lists the threads the user sent to you (to this agent, across notes). On one note threads on the note as a whole (kind "note") come first, then the rest in the order of the text, orphans last (their text was deleted; the quote stays). Each says where it is now (position: the text there, whether it still matchesQuote, the headings it is under, its block number; for an orphan, whether it was found again by its text and how). Each thread is a summary (its quote, state, how many comments and who wrote the last): read one with read_comment_thread for its comments.

title: Read a comment thread
description: Read one thread with all its comments, each naming its author (the user, or an agent). The quote is the text the thread is on (kind "note": the note as a whole, no quote). position is where it is now: text (a range’s text there now), matchesQuote, headings (outermost first), block (the nth block of text) and paragraph (that block’s text now); found is "anchor", or for a thread whose text was deleted "refound" (found again by its quote and the text around it; how: exact, exact-context, fuzzy or context, with similarity) or "lost". context is where it was when it was made: the text just before and after it, its headings, block and paragraph then. read_note gives the whole note. Reading a thread the user sent to you tells them you have seen it.
